passages.translation: Objective: To evaluate the homologous recombination repair deficiency (HRD) status of ovarian cancer patients by next-generation sequencing (NGS) technology and analyze its correlation with clinicopathological features, microsatellite instability (MSI) and tumor mutational burden (TMB), providing a basis for genetic risk assessment, PARP inhibitor (PARPi) precision therapy and prognostic management of ovarian cancer. Methods: 182 ovarian cancer patients who underwent HRD testing at Xiangya Second Hospital of Central South University from January 2021 to August 2025 were collected. NGS technology was used to detect germline and somatic mutations in breast cancer-related genes (BRCA) 1/2 and other genes, HRD score, MSI and TMB. HRD positivity was defined as the presence of BRCA1/2 pathogenic/likely pathogenic mutations and/or positive HRD score. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) was used to detect the expression of mismatch repair proteins and p53. Results: The HRD positive rate of 182 patients was 65.38% (119/182), and the HRD score positive rate was 53.30% (97/182).
